class MenuItem(BitmappySprite):
    """A menu item class.

    This class represents a menu item.  It can be a root level menu item or a sub menu item.

    """

    log = LOG

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        x: float = 0,
        y: float = 0,
        width: float = 1,
        height: float = 1,
        *,
        name: str | None = None,
        filename: str | None = None,
        parent: object | None = None,
        groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize a MenuItem.

        Args:
            x (int | float): The x coordinate of the menu item.
            y (int | float): The y coordinate of the menu item.
            width (int | float): The width of the menu item.
            height (int | float): The height of the menu item.
            name (str | None): The name of the menu item.
            filename (str | None): The filename of the menu item.
            parent (object | None): The parent of the menu item.
            groups (pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] | None): The sprite groups to add the sprite to.

        """
        if groups is None:
            groups = pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty()

        super().__init__(
            x=x,
            y=y,
            width=width,
            height=height,
            name=name,
            focusable=True,
            filename=filename,
            groups=groups,
        )
        self.all_sprites: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] = groups

        self.log.debug('MENUITEM GROUPS: %s', groups)

        self.background_color: tuple[int, ...] = (255, 0, 255)
        self.border_width: int = 2
        self.menu_items: dict[str | None, MenuItem] = {}
        self.menu_offset_x: int = self.border_width
        self.menu_offset_y: int = self.border_width
        self.menu_image: pygame.Surface = pygame.Surface((0, 0))
        self.menu_rect: pygame.FRect | pygame.Rect = pygame.Rect(0, 0, 0, 0)
        self.menu_down_image: pygame.Surface = pygame.Surface((0, 0))
        self.menu_down_rect: pygame.FRect | pygame.Rect = pygame.Rect(0, 0, 0, 0)
        self.menu_up_image: pygame.Surface = pygame.Surface((0, 0))
        self.menu_up_rect: pygame.FRect | pygame.Rect = pygame.Rect(0, 0, 0, 0)
        self.is_active: bool = False
        self.name = name
        self.parent = parent

        # Don't set a name for the icon.
        if self.name:
            # Avoid circular import: TextSprite is in text_widgets.py
            from glitchygames.ui.text_widgets import TextSprite

            self.image.fill((255, 255, 255))
            self.image.set_colorkey((255, 255, 255))
            self.text = TextSprite(
                background_color=(255, 255, 255),  # White background to match menu
                text_color=(0, 0, 0),
                x=x,
                y=y,
                width=self.width,
                height=self.height,
                text=self.name,
                parent=parent,
                groups=groups,
            )
            # Align the rect with the text position
            self.rect.x = self.text.rect.x
            self.rect.y = self.text.rect.y

        self.menu_up_image = self.image
        self.menu_up_rect = self.rect
        self.menu_down_image = self.menu_up_image
        self.menu_down_rect = self.menu_up_rect

    @override
    def add(self: Self, *groups: Any) -> None:
        """Add the sprite to a group.

        Args:
            *groups: The groups to add the sprite to.

        """
        # There's something funky with MRO and pygame
        # doing things this way avoids dirtier tricks.
        try:
            text = getattr(self, 'text')  # ruff: ignore[get-attr-with-constant]
            text.add(*groups)
        except AttributeError:
            pass

    def add_menu(self: Self, menu: MenuItem) -> None:
        """Add a menu to the menu item.

        Args:
            menu (MenuItem): The menu to add.

        """
        menu.image.set_colorkey((255, 0, 255))
        menu.add(self.groups())
        menu.add(self.all_sprites)
        if not len(self.menu_items.keys()):
            self.menu_offset_y += int(self.rect.height)
        else:
            menu.rect.x += self.menu_offset_x
            menu.rect.y += self.menu_offset_y
            self.menu_offset_y += int(menu.rect.height)

        self.menu_items[menu.name] = menu  # ty: ignore[invalid-assignment]

        # Now recreate the menu image for later use.
        self.menu_image = pygame.Surface((400, 300))
        self.menu_image.convert()
        self.menu_image.set_colorkey((255, 0, 255))
        self.menu_image.fill((255, 255, 255))
        self.menu_rect = self.menu_image.get_rect()
        self.menu_rect.x = self.rect.x
        self.menu_rect.y = 21

        # A sub-menu without a rect takes no room; with none, the dropped-down menu keeps this
        # item's own size (max() over no rects raised ValueError: BUGS.md #136)
        menu_rects = [
            self.menu_items[mi].rect
            for mi in self.menu_items
            if self.menu_items[mi].rect is not None  # pyright: ignore[reportUnnecessaryComparison]
        ]
        width = max((r.width + 20) for r in menu_rects) * 2.5 if menu_rects else self.rect.width
        heights = [r.height for r in menu_rects]
        height = self.rect.height

        if heights:
            self.log.debug('Heights: %s', heights)
            heights.append(self.rect.height)
            self.log.debug('New Heights: %s', heights)
            height = sum(heights)

        # Create a new image that is self.height + [menu.height for menu in self.menu_items]
        # Create a new image that is self.width + [menu.width for menu in self.menu_items]
        self.menu_down_image = pygame.Surface((width, height))
        self.menu_down_image.set_colorkey((255, 0, 255))
        self.menu_down_rect = self.menu_down_image.get_rect()
        self.menu_down_rect.x = self.rect.x
        self.menu_down_rect.y = self.rect.y
        self.menu_down_image.fill((255, 255, 255))
        self.rect.width = self.menu_down_rect.width
        self.rect.height = self.menu_down_rect.height

        # Put ourselves at the top of the list.
        self.menu_down_image.blit(self.image, (0, self.rect.y))

        y_offset = self.rect.height
        for menu_name in self.menu_items:
            menu_item = self.menu_items[menu_name]
            if menu_item.rect is None:  # pyright: ignore[reportUnnecessaryComparison]
                continue
            menu_item.rect.y = y_offset
            menu_item.rect.width = menu_item.text.width
            menu_item.rect.height = menu_item.text.height
            self.menu_down_image.blit(menu_item.image, (menu_item.rect.x, menu_item.rect.y))
            y_offset += menu_item.rect.height

    def add_menu_item(self: Self, menu_item: MenuItem, menu: MenuBar | None) -> None:
        """Add a menu item to the menu item.

        Args:
            menu_item (MenuItem): The menu item to add.
            menu (MenuBar): The menu to add the menu item to.

        """
        if menu is None:
            self.add_menu(menu=menu_item)
            self.log.debug('%s Adding new menu %s.', type(self), menu_item)
        else:
            self.log.debug('%s Adding menu item %s to menu %s.', type(self), menu_item, menu)

    @override
    def update(self: Self) -> None:
        """Update the menu item."""
        # Draw to our own surface instead of the screen
        if self.is_active and self.menu_image and self.menu_rect:
            self.log.debug('Drawing the menu')
            self.image.blit(self.menu_image, (0, 0))  # Draw relative to our own surface

    @override
    def on_left_mouse_drag_event(
        self: Self, event: MouseMotionEvent, trigger: MouseButtonEvent
    ) -> None:
        """Handle left mouse drag events.

        Args:
            event (MouseMotionEvent): The event to handle.
            trigger (object): The trigger object.

        """
        # Not logged: a drag arrives with every mouse motion while a button is held, so a log
        # line here would run every frame of a drag and drown out useful debug output.

    @override
    def on_left_mouse_drop_event(
        self: Self, event: MouseButtonEvent, trigger: MouseButtonEvent
    ) -> None:
        """Handle left mouse drop events.

        Args:
            event (MouseButtonEvent): The event to handle.
            trigger (object): The trigger object.

        """
        self.log.debug('%s Mouse Drop %s', type(self), self.name)

    @override
    def on_middle_mouse_drag_event(
        self: Self,
        event: MouseMotionEvent,
        trigger: MouseButtonEvent,
    ) -> None:
        """Handle middle mouse drag events.

        Args:
            event (MouseMotionEvent): The event to handle.
            trigger (object): The trigger object.

        """
        # Not logged: a drag arrives with every mouse motion while a button is held, so a log
        # line here would run every frame of a drag and drown out useful debug output.

    @override
    def on_middle_mouse_drop_event(
        self: Self,
        event: MouseButtonEvent,
        trigger: MouseButtonEvent,
    ) -> None:
        """Handle middle mouse drop events.

        Args:
            event (MouseButtonEvent): The event to handle.
            trigger (object): The trigger object.

        """
        self.log.debug('%s Mouse Drop %s', type(self), self.name)

    @override
    def on_mouse_drag_event(self: Self, event: MouseMotionEvent, trigger: MouseButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Handle mouse drag events.

        Args:
            event (MouseMotionEvent): The event to handle.
            trigger (object): The trigger object.

        """
        # Not logged: a drag arrives with every mouse motion while a button is held, so a log
        # line here would run every frame of a drag and drown out useful debug output.

    @override
    def on_mouse_drop_event(self: Self, event: MouseButtonEvent, trigger: MouseButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Handle mouse drop events.

        Args:
            event (MouseButtonEvent): The event to handle.
            trigger (object): The trigger object.

        """
        self.log.debug('%s Mouse Drop %s', type(self), self.name)

    @override
    def on_mouse_motion_event(self: Self, event: MouseMotionEvent) -> None:
        """Handle mouse motion events.

        Args:
            event (MouseMotionEvent): The event to handle.

        """
        mouse = MousePointer(pos=event.pos)

        collided_sprites = pygame.sprite.spritecollide(
            sprite=mouse,
            group=self.all_sprites,
            dokill=False,
        )

        for collided_sprite in collided_sprites:
            if collided_sprite.name in self.menu_items:
                self.log.debug(
                    'Mouse enter on %s %s at %s',
                    collided_sprite.name,
                    collided_sprite.rect,
                    mouse.rect,
                )
                collided_sprite.on_mouse_motion_event(event)

                # menu_items maps names to items: iterate the items (iterating the dict gave
                # the names, strings without handlers)
                for submenu in collided_sprite.menu_items.values():
                    submenu.on_mouse_motion_event(event)

        self.has_focus = False

    @override
    def on_mouse_enter_event(self: Self, event: HashableEvent) -> None:
        """Handle mouse enter events.

        Args:
            event (pygame.event.Event): The event to handle.

        """
        self.log.debug('%s ENTER MENU %s', type(self), self.name)
        # Figure out which item was entered.
        mouse = MousePointer(pos=event.pos)

        collided_sprites = pygame.sprite.spritecollide(
            sprite=mouse,
            group=self.all_sprites,
            dokill=False,
        )

        for collided_sprite in collided_sprites:
            # Click the menu item.
            #
            # Don't click sub menus.
            if collided_sprite.name in self.menu_items:
                self.log.debug(
                    'Mouse enter on %s %s at %s',
                    collided_sprite.name,
                    collided_sprite.rect,
                    mouse.rect,
                )
                collided_sprite.on_mouse_enter_event(event)

                for submenu in collided_sprite.menu_items.values():
                    submenu.on_mouse_enter_event(event)

        self.has_focus = True

    @override
    def on_mouse_exit_event(self: Self, event: HashableEvent) -> None:
        """Handle mouse exit events.

        Args:
            event (pygame.event.Event): The event to handle.

        """
        # Figure out which item was entered.
        mouse = MousePointer(pos=event.pos)

        collided_sprites = pygame.sprite.spritecollide(
            sprite=mouse,
            group=self.all_sprites,
            dokill=False,
        )

        for collided_sprite in collided_sprites:
            # Click the menu item.
            #
            # Don't click sub menus.
            if collided_sprite.name in self.menu_items:
                self.log.debug(
                    'Mouse exit on %s %s at %s',
                    collided_sprite.name,
                    collided_sprite.rect,
                    mouse,
                )
                collided_sprite.on_mouse_exit_event(event)

                # Leaving the item leaves its sub-items too (this sent them an enter event)
                for submenu in collided_sprite.menu_items.values():
                    submenu.on_mouse_exit_event(event)

        self.has_focus = False
        self.dirty = 1

    @override
    def on_left_mouse_button_up_event(self: Self, event: MouseButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Handle left mouse button up events.

        Args:
            event (MouseButtonEvent): The event to handle.

        """
        self.log.debug('%s Mouse Up %s', type(self), self.name)
        self.image = self.menu_up_image
        self.rect = self.menu_up_rect
        self.is_active = False
        self.dirty = 2
        self.update()

        # Figure out which item was clicked.
        mouse = MousePointer(pos=event.pos)

        self.log.debug('Process MOUSE UP %s at %s', event, mouse)

        sprites = pygame.sprite.spritecollide(sprite=mouse, group=self.all_sprites, dokill=False)

        for sprite in sprites:
            # Click the menu item.
            #
            # Don't click sub menus.
            # if sprite.name in self.menu_items:
            if isinstance(sprite, MenuItem):
                self.log.debug('Mouse button up on %s at %s', sprite.name, mouse.rect)

                self.log.debug(
                    '%s Clicked Menu Item: Name: %s, '
                    'Width: %s,'
                    'Height: %s, '
                    'Clicked X: %s, Clicked Y: %s,'
                    'my X: %s, '
                    'my Y: %s',
                    type(self),
                    sprite.name,
                    sprite.rect.width,
                    sprite.rect.height,
                    mouse.rect.x,
                    mouse.rect.y,
                    sprite.rect.x,
                    sprite.rect.y,
                )
                menu_item_callback = sprite.callbacks.get('on_menu_item_event', None)

                if menu_item_callback:
                    menu_item_callback(self, event)
                # Create a menu item clicked event.
                # Emit it to the pygame event subsystem.
                post_event(
                    pygame.event.Event(events.MENUEVENT, {'menu': self, 'menu_item': sprite}),
                )

    @override
    def on_left_mouse_button_down_event(self: Self, event: MouseButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Handle left mouse button down events.

        Args:
            event (MouseButtonEvent): The event to handle.

        """
        self.log.debug('%s Mouse Down %s', type(self), self.name)
        self.image = self.menu_down_image
        self.rect = self.menu_down_rect
        self.is_active = True
        self.dirty = 2

        self.update()

        # Figure out which item was clicked.
        mouse = MousePointer(pos=event.pos)

        collided_sprites = pygame.sprite.spritecollide(
            sprite=mouse,
            group=self.all_sprites,
            dokill=False,
        )

        for collided_sprite in collided_sprites:
            # Click the menu item.
            #
            # Don't click sub menus.
            if collided_sprite.name in self.menu_items:
                clicked_sprite: object = collided_sprite
                self.log.debug(
                    '%s Mouse button down on %s at %s',
                    type(clicked_sprite),
                    collided_sprite.name,
                    mouse.rect,
                )
                collided_sprite.on_left_mouse_button_down_event(event)

    @override
    def on_right_mouse_drag_event(
        self: Self,
        event: MouseMotionEvent,
        trigger: MouseButtonEvent | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Handle right mouse drag events.

        Args:
            event (MouseMotionEvent): The event to handle.
            trigger (HashableEvent | None): The object that triggered the event.

        """
        # Not logged: a drag arrives with every mouse motion while a button is held, so a log
        # line here would run every frame of a drag and drown out useful debug output.

    @override
    def on_right_mouse_drop_event(
        self: Self,
        event: MouseButtonEvent,
        trigger: MouseButtonEvent | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Handle right mouse drop events.

        Args:
            event (MouseButtonEvent): The event to handle.
            trigger (HashableEvent | None): The object that triggered the event.

        """
        self.log.debug('%s Mouse Drop %s', type(self), self.name)

    @override
    def on_mouse_wheel_event(
        self: Self,
        event: MouseWheelEvent,
        trigger: HashableEvent | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Handle mouse wheel events.

        Args:
            event (MouseWheelEvent): The event to handle.
            trigger (HashableEvent | None): The object that triggered the event.

        """
        self.log.debug('%s Mouse Wheel %s', type(self), self.name)

def __init__(
    self: Self,
    x: float = 0,
    y: float = 0,
    width: float = 1,
    height: float = 1,
    *,
    name: str | None = None,
    filename: str | None = None,
    parent: object | None = None,
    groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Initialize a MenuItem.

    Args:
        x (int | float): The x coordinate of the menu item.
        y (int | float): The y coordinate of the menu item.
        width (int | float): The width of the menu item.
        height (int | float): The height of the menu item.
        name (str | None): The name of the menu item.
        filename (str | None): The filename of the menu item.
        parent (object | None): The parent of the menu item.
        groups (pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] | None): The sprite groups to add the sprite to.

    """
    if groups is None:
        groups = pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty()

    super().__init__(
        x=x,
        y=y,
        width=width,
        height=height,
        name=name,
        focusable=True,
        filename=filename,
        groups=groups,
    )
    self.all_sprites: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] = groups

    self.log.debug('MENUITEM GROUPS: %s', groups)

    self.background_color: tuple[int, ...] = (255, 0, 255)
    self.border_width: int = 2
    self.menu_items: dict[str | None, MenuItem] = {}
    self.menu_offset_x: int = self.border_width
    self.menu_offset_y: int = self.border_width
    self.menu_image: pygame.Surface = pygame.Surface((0, 0))
    self.menu_rect: pygame.FRect | pygame.Rect = pygame.Rect(0, 0, 0, 0)
    self.menu_down_image: pygame.Surface = pygame.Surface((0, 0))
    self.menu_down_rect: pygame.FRect | pygame.Rect = pygame.Rect(0, 0, 0, 0)
    self.menu_up_image: pygame.Surface = pygame.Surface((0, 0))
    self.menu_up_rect: pygame.FRect | pygame.Rect = pygame.Rect(0, 0, 0, 0)
    self.is_active: bool = False
    self.name = name
    self.parent = parent

    # Don't set a name for the icon.
    if self.name:
        # Avoid circular import: TextSprite is in text_widgets.py
        from glitchygames.ui.text_widgets import TextSprite

        self.image.fill((255, 255, 255))
        self.image.set_colorkey((255, 255, 255))
        self.text = TextSprite(
            background_color=(255, 255, 255),  # White background to match menu
            text_color=(0, 0, 0),
            x=x,
            y=y,
            width=self.width,
            height=self.height,
            text=self.name,
            parent=parent,
            groups=groups,
        )
        # Align the rect with the text position
        self.rect.x = self.text.rect.x
        self.rect.y = self.text.rect.y

    self.menu_up_image = self.image
    self.menu_up_rect = self.rect
    self.menu_down_image = self.menu_up_image
    self.menu_down_rect = self.menu_up_rect

@override
def add(self: Self, *groups: Any) -> None:
    """Add the sprite to a group.

    Args:
        *groups: The groups to add the sprite to.

    """
    # There's something funky with MRO and pygame
    # doing things this way avoids dirtier tricks.
    try:
        text = getattr(self, 'text')  # ruff: ignore[get-attr-with-constant]
        text.add(*groups)
    except AttributeError:
        pass

def add_menu(self: Self, menu: MenuItem) -> None:
    """Add a menu to the menu item.

    Args:
        menu (MenuItem): The menu to add.

    """
    menu.image.set_colorkey((255, 0, 255))
    menu.add(self.groups())
    menu.add(self.all_sprites)
    if not len(self.menu_items.keys()):
        self.menu_offset_y += int(self.rect.height)
    else:
        menu.rect.x += self.menu_offset_x
        menu.rect.y += self.menu_offset_y
        self.menu_offset_y += int(menu.rect.height)

    self.menu_items[menu.name] = menu  # ty: ignore[invalid-assignment]

    # Now recreate the menu image for later use.
    self.menu_image = pygame.Surface((400, 300))
    self.menu_image.convert()
    self.menu_image.set_colorkey((255, 0, 255))
    self.menu_image.fill((255, 255, 255))
    self.menu_rect = self.menu_image.get_rect()
    self.menu_rect.x = self.rect.x
    self.menu_rect.y = 21

    # A sub-menu without a rect takes no room; with none, the dropped-down menu keeps this
    # item's own size (max() over no rects raised ValueError: BUGS.md #136)
    menu_rects = [
        self.menu_items[mi].rect
        for mi in self.menu_items
        if self.menu_items[mi].rect is not None  # pyright: ignore[reportUnnecessaryComparison]
    ]
    width = max((r.width + 20) for r in menu_rects) * 2.5 if menu_rects else self.rect.width
    heights = [r.height for r in menu_rects]
    height = self.rect.height

    if heights:
        self.log.debug('Heights: %s', heights)
        heights.append(self.rect.height)
        self.log.debug('New Heights: %s', heights)
        height = sum(heights)

    # Create a new image that is self.height + [menu.height for menu in self.menu_items]
    # Create a new image that is self.width + [menu.width for menu in self.menu_items]
    self.menu_down_image = pygame.Surface((width, height))
    self.menu_down_image.set_colorkey((255, 0, 255))
    self.menu_down_rect = self.menu_down_image.get_rect()
    self.menu_down_rect.x = self.rect.x
    self.menu_down_rect.y = self.rect.y
    self.menu_down_image.fill((255, 255, 255))
    self.rect.width = self.menu_down_rect.width
    self.rect.height = self.menu_down_rect.height

    # Put ourselves at the top of the list.
    self.menu_down_image.blit(self.image, (0, self.rect.y))

    y_offset = self.rect.height
    for menu_name in self.menu_items:
        menu_item = self.menu_items[menu_name]
        if menu_item.rect is None:  # pyright: ignore[reportUnnecessaryComparison]
            continue
        menu_item.rect.y = y_offset
        menu_item.rect.width = menu_item.text.width
        menu_item.rect.height = menu_item.text.height
        self.menu_down_image.blit(menu_item.image, (menu_item.rect.x, menu_item.rect.y))
        y_offset += menu_item.rect.height

@override
def on_mouse_enter_event(self: Self, event: HashableEvent) -> None:
    """Handle mouse enter events.

    Args:
        event (pygame.event.Event): The event to handle.

    """
    self.log.debug('%s ENTER MENU %s', type(self), self.name)
    # Figure out which item was entered.
    mouse = MousePointer(pos=event.pos)

    collided_sprites = pygame.sprite.spritecollide(
        sprite=mouse,
        group=self.all_sprites,
        dokill=False,
    )

    for collided_sprite in collided_sprites:
        # Click the menu item.
        #
        # Don't click sub menus.
        if collided_sprite.name in self.menu_items:
            self.log.debug(
                'Mouse enter on %s %s at %s',
                collided_sprite.name,
                collided_sprite.rect,
                mouse.rect,
            )
            collided_sprite.on_mouse_enter_event(event)

            for submenu in collided_sprite.menu_items.values():
                submenu.on_mouse_enter_event(event)

    self.has_focus = True

def on_mouse_exit_event(self: Self, event: HashableEvent) -> None:
    """Handle mouse exit events.

    Args:
        event (pygame.event.Event): The event to handle.

    """
    # Figure out which item was entered.
    mouse = MousePointer(pos=event.pos)

    collided_sprites = pygame.sprite.spritecollide(
        sprite=mouse,
        group=self.all_sprites,
        dokill=False,
    )

    for collided_sprite in collided_sprites:

        # Don't click sub menus.

                'Mouse exit on %s %s at %s',
                collided_sprite.name,
                collided_sprite.rect,
                mouse,
            )
            collided_sprite.on_mouse_exit_event(event)

            # Leaving the item leaves its sub-items too (this sent them an enter event)
            for submenu in collided_sprite.menu_items.values():
                submenu.on_mouse_exit_event(event)

    self.has_focus = False
    self.dirty = 1

A message centred over a dimmed picture of the game: the pause screen's look, shared.

MessageScreen is the one drawing path for "pause-style message over the game": the pause screen (glitchygames/scenes/builtin_scenes/pause_scene.py) draws its PAUSED with it, and the watched replay's start screen (glitchygames/replay/controls.py) is a subclass that changes the message and the look and adds a smaller hint line under the message. A subclass changes only the class attributes (and hint_text for a hint worked out at draw time).

MessageScreen #

Draws a centred message (and an optional hint line under it) over a dimmed surface.

The defaults are the pause screen's look: the whole surface dimmed with black at alpha 128, then PAUSED in pygame's default font at size 72, white, centred on the surface. Fonts and rendered text are made on the first draw and reused, so drawing every frame costs blits only.

Attributes:
  • MESSAGE (str) –

    The message, centred on the surface.

  • MESSAGE_FONT_PATH (Path | None) –

    The message's font file, or None for pygame's default font.

  • MESSAGE_FONT_SIZE (int) –

    The message's font size.

  • MESSAGE_COLOR (tuple[int, int, int]) –

    The message's colour.

  • HINT_FONT_PATH (Path | None) –

    The hint line's font file, or None for pygame's default font.

  • HINT_FONT_SIZE (int) –

    The hint line's font size.

  • HINT_COLOR (tuple[int, int, int]) –

    The hint line's colour.

  • HINT_GAP (int) –

    Pixels between the message's bottom and the hint line's top.

  • DIM_COLOR (tuple[int, int, int]) –

    The colour laid over the whole surface.

  • DIM_ALPHA (int) –

    How opaque that colour is (0-255).

class MessageScreen:
    """Draws a centred message (and an optional hint line under it) over a dimmed surface.

    The defaults are the pause screen's look: the whole surface dimmed with black at alpha 128,
    then ``PAUSED`` in pygame's default font at size 72, white, centred on the surface. Fonts and
    rendered text are made on the first draw and reused, so drawing every frame costs blits only.

    Attributes:
        MESSAGE: The message, centred on the surface.
        MESSAGE_FONT_PATH: The message's font file, or None for pygame's default font.
        MESSAGE_FONT_SIZE: The message's font size.
        MESSAGE_COLOR: The message's colour.
        HINT_FONT_PATH: The hint line's font file, or None for pygame's default font.
        HINT_FONT_SIZE: The hint line's font size.
        HINT_COLOR: The hint line's colour.
        HINT_GAP: Pixels between the message's bottom and the hint line's top.
        DIM_COLOR: The colour laid over the whole surface.
        DIM_ALPHA: How opaque that colour is (0-255).

    """

    MESSAGE: ClassVar[str] = 'PAUSED'
    MESSAGE_FONT_PATH: ClassVar[Path | None] = None
    MESSAGE_FONT_SIZE: ClassVar[int] = 72
    MESSAGE_COLOR: ClassVar[tuple[int, int, int]] = WHITE
    HINT_FONT_PATH: ClassVar[Path | None] = None
    HINT_FONT_SIZE: ClassVar[int] = 24
    HINT_COLOR: ClassVar[tuple[int, int, int]] = WHITE
    HINT_GAP: ClassVar[int] = 16
    DIM_COLOR: ClassVar[tuple[int, int, int]] = BLACK
    DIM_ALPHA: ClassVar[int] = 128

    def __init__(self: Self) -> None:
        """Prepare the screen; fonts and text are made on the first draw."""
        self._message_surface: pygame.Surface | None = None
        self._hint_surface: pygame.Surface | None = None
        self._rendered_hint: str | None = None
        # The dimming layer, kept for the size it was made for
        self._dim_surface: pygame.Surface | None = None

    def hint_text(self: Self) -> str | None:
        """Return the smaller line drawn under the message (none on the pause screen).

        Returns:
            The hint, or None for no hint line.

        """
        return None

    def render(
        self: Self, *, backdrop: pygame.Surface, area_size: tuple[int, int] | None = None
    ) -> pygame.Surface:
        """Return a copy of ``backdrop`` with the screen drawn over it.

        Args:
            backdrop: The picture of the game (left unchanged).
            area_size: The (width, height) dimmed and centred on, from the top-left corner;
                None for the backdrop's own size.

        Returns:
            The new surface.

        """
        image = backdrop.copy()
        self.draw(surface=image, area_size=area_size)
        return image

    def draw(
        self: Self, *, surface: pygame.Surface, area_size: tuple[int, int] | None = None
    ) -> None:
        """Dim ``surface``, then draw the message centred on it and the hint line under it.

        Args:
            surface: The surface to draw onto (changed in place).
            area_size: The (width, height) dimmed and centred on, from the top-left corner;
                None for the surface's own size (the pause screen passes the game's screen
                size, which a custom screenshot need not have).

        """
        size = surface.get_size() if area_size is None else area_size
        surface.blit(self._dimming_layer(size=size), (0, 0))
        message_rect, hint_rect = self.text_rects(size=size)
        surface.blit(self._message(), message_rect)
        hint_surface = self._hint()
        if hint_surface is not None and hint_rect is not None:
            surface.blit(hint_surface, hint_rect)

    def text_rects(self: Self, *, size: tuple[int, int]) -> tuple[pygame.Rect, pygame.Rect | None]:
        """Return where the message and the hint line go on a surface of ``size``.

        Args:
            size: The surface's (width, height).

        Returns:
            The message's rect, centred on the surface, and the hint line's rect, centred
            horizontally ``HINT_GAP`` pixels under the message (None without a hint).

        """
        width, height = size
        message_rect = self._message().get_rect()
        message_rect.center = (width // 2, height // 2)
        hint_surface = self._hint()
        if hint_surface is None:
            return message_rect, None
        hint_rect = hint_surface.get_rect()
        hint_rect.midtop = (width // 2, message_rect.bottom + self.HINT_GAP)
        return message_rect, hint_rect

    def _message(self: Self) -> pygame.Surface:
        if self._message_surface is None:
            font = pygame.font.Font(self.MESSAGE_FONT_PATH, self.MESSAGE_FONT_SIZE)
            self._message_surface = font.render(
                self.MESSAGE, antialias=True, color=self.MESSAGE_COLOR
            )
        return self._message_surface

    def _hint(self: Self) -> pygame.Surface | None:
        hint = self.hint_text()
        if hint is None:
            return None
        if self._hint_surface is None or hint != self._rendered_hint:
            font = pygame.font.Font(self.HINT_FONT_PATH, self.HINT_FONT_SIZE)
            self._hint_surface = font.render(hint, antialias=True, color=self.HINT_COLOR)
            self._rendered_hint = hint
        return self._hint_surface

    def _dimming_layer(self: Self, *, size: tuple[int, int]) -> pygame.Surface:
        if self._dim_surface is None or self._dim_surface.get_size() != size:
            self._dim_surface = pygame.Surface(size)
            self._dim_surface.fill(self.DIM_COLOR)
            self._dim_surface.set_alpha(self.DIM_ALPHA)
        return self._dim_surface

class ColorWellSprite(BitmappySprite):
    """A color well sprite class."""

    log = LOG

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        x: int,
        y: int,
        width: int,
        height: int,
        name: str,
        *,
        parent: object | None = None,
        groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize a ColorWellSprite.

        Args:
            x (int): The x coordinate of the color well sprite.
            y (int): The y coordinate of the color well sprite.
            width (int): The width of the color well sprite.
            height (int): The height of the color well sprite.
            name (str): The name of the color well sprite.
            parent (object): The parent object.
            groups (pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] | None): The sprite groups to add the sprite to.

        """
        if groups is None:
            groups = pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty()

        super().__init__(
            x=x,
            y=y,
            width=width,
            height=height,
            name=name,
            parent=parent,
            groups=groups,
        )

        # Override the surface to support alpha
        self.image = pygame.Surface((width, height), pygame.SRCALPHA)

        self.red = 0
        self.green = 0
        self.blue = 0
        self.alpha = 255

    @property
    def active_color(self: Self) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
        """The active color.

        Returns:
            tuple[R: int, G: int, B: int, A: int]: The active color.

        """
        return (self.red, self.green, self.blue, self.alpha)

    @active_color.setter
    def active_color(
        self: Self,
        active_color: tuple[int, int, int] | tuple[int, int, int, int],
    ) -> None:
        """Set the active color.

        Args:
            active_color: The new active color as
                (R, G, B) or (R, G, B, A) tuple.

        """
        self.red = active_color[0]
        self.green = active_color[1]
        self.blue = active_color[2]
        # Handle both RGB and RGBA tuples
        if len(active_color) == RGBA_COMPONENT_COUNT:
            self.alpha = active_color[3]
        else:
            self.alpha = 255  # Default to fully opaque if not specified
        self.dirty = 1

    @override
    def update_nested_sprites(self: Self) -> None:
        """Update the nested sprites."""

    @override
    def update(self: Self) -> None:
        """Update the color well sprite."""
        pygame.draw.rect(self.image, (128, 128, 255), Rect(0, 0, self.width, self.height), 1)

        # Draw the color directly on the alpha-compatible surface
        pygame.draw.rect(self.image, self.active_color, Rect(1, 1, self.width - 2, self.height - 2))

class SliderSprite(BitmappySprite):
    """A slider sprite class."""

    log = logging.getLogger('game')

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        x: int,
        y: int,
        width: int = 256,
        height: int = 9,
        *,
        name: str | None = None,
        parent: SliderProtocol | None = None,
        groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize a SliderSprite.

        Args:
            x (int): The x coordinate of the slider sprite.
            y (int): The y coordinate of the slider sprite.
            width (int): The width of the slider sprite.
            height (int): The height of the slider sprite.
            name (str): The name of the slider sprite.
            parent (SliderProtocol | None): The parent object.
            groups (pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] | None): The sprite groups to add the sprite to.

        """
        if groups is None:
            groups = pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty()

        # self.log is the class-level SliderSprite.log (logging.getLogger('game')).
        self.log.info('Initializing slider %s with parent %s', name, parent)

        super().__init__(
            x=x,
            y=y,
            width=width,
            height=height,
            name=name,
            focusable=True,
            parent=parent,
            groups=groups,
        )

        # Initialize base values
        self._value = 0
        self.dragging = False

        # Initialize the slider knob
        self.slider_knob = BitmappySprite(
            x=x,
            y=y,
            width=5,
            height=height,
            name=f'{name}_knob',
            groups=groups,
        )
        self.slider_knob.image.fill((200, 200, 200))

        # Create text sprite and event handlers
        self._init_text_sprite(x, y, width, height, groups)

        # Ensure slider rect is properly set for mouse detection
        self.rect = pygame.Rect(x, y, width, height)

        # The knob's left edge runs from the slider's left edge to 5 pixels (its width) short
        # of the right edge
        self.min_x = x
        self.max_x = x + width - 5

        # The track's gradient as last drawn, kept to repaint the image with (see
        # _current_gradient), and the image, size and name it was drawn for
        self._gradient: pygame.Surface | None = None
        self._gradient_drawn_on: pygame.Surface | None = None
        # The name is compared only; Sprite falls back to the class as a name (sprite.py)
        self._gradient_drawn_for: tuple[int | float, int | float, object] | None = None

        # Set up appearance
        self.update_slider_appearance()

        # Make sure we update
        self.dirty = 2
        self.slider_knob.dirty = 2

        # Now set the initial value
        self.value = self._value

    @property
    def value(self) -> int:
        """The slider value."""
        return self._value

    @value.setter
    def value(self, new_value: int) -> None:
        """Set the slider value, move the knob and show the value in the text box's format.

        Setting the value ends any editing in the text box.
        """
        # __init__ makes the knob and the text sprite before it first sets the value
        self._value = max(0, min(MAX_COLOR_CHANNEL_VALUE, new_value))
        self.slider_knob.rect.x = self.min_x + (
            self._value * (self.max_x - self.min_x) // MAX_COLOR_CHANNEL_VALUE
        )
        self.slider_knob.dirty = 2
        # Deactivate text sprite and update text
        self.text_sprite.is_active = False
        self.text_sprite.text = format_channel(self._value, self.input_format)
        self.text_sprite.update_text(self.text_sprite.text)
        self.text_sprite.dirty = 2  # Force redraw

    @property
    def input_format(self) -> str:
        """The text box format: the parent's slider_input_format, decimal without a parent."""
        return getattr(self.parent, 'slider_input_format', DECIMAL_INPUT_FORMAT)

    def _init_text_sprite(
        self,
        x: int,
        y: int,
        width: int,
        height: int,
        groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any],
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the text sprite and its event handlers."""
        text_x = x + width + 4  # 4 pixel gap to prevent overlap
        # Center the text sprite vertically with the slider's center, moved down 2 pixels
        text_height = 20
        slider_center_y = y + height // 2
        text_y = slider_center_y - text_height // 2 + 2

        # Calculate text box width to fit between slider end and color well start
        # This will be set by the parent scene after color well is created
        text_width = 44  # Default width, will be updated by parent scene (4 pixels wider)

        self.text_sprite = TextSprite(
            x=text_x,
            y=text_y,
            width=text_width,
            height=text_height,
            text='0',
            background_color=(0, 0, 0),  # Solid black background like color well
            groups=groups,
        )
        # Make text sprite interactive for editing
        self.text_sprite.focusable = True
        self.text_sprite.is_active = False  # Start inactive

        # Store original value for restoration
        self.original_value = self._value

        # Add keyboard event handling for text input
        def handle_text_input(event: HashableEvent) -> None:
            if not self.text_sprite.is_active:
                return
            if event.key == pygame.K_RETURN:
                self.commit_text(event=event)
            elif event.key == pygame.K_ESCAPE:
                self._restore_original_value()
            elif (
                event.unicode.isdigit()
                or event.unicode.lower() in HEX_DIGIT_LETTERS
                or event.key == pygame.K_BACKSPACE
            ):
                self._handle_text_character_input(event)

        self.text_sprite.on_key_down_event = handle_text_input  # ty: ignore[invalid-assignment]

        # Add mouse click handling to activate text editing
        def handle_text_click(event: HashableEvent) -> bool:
            if self.text_sprite.rect.collidepoint(event.pos):
                # Store current value as original for restoration
                self.original_value = self._value
                # Clear the text box for editing
                self.text_sprite.text = ''
                self.text_sprite.is_active = True
                self.text_sprite.update_text(self.text_sprite.text)
                self.text_sprite.dirty = 2
                return True
            return False

        self.text_sprite.on_left_mouse_button_down_event = handle_text_click  # type: ignore[assignment] # ty: ignore[invalid-assignment]

    def _restore_original_value(self) -> None:
        """Restore the slider text to its original value, in the active format, and deactivate.

        It was always written in decimal, even on the hex tab.
        """
        self.text_sprite.text = format_channel(self.original_value, self.input_format)
        self.text_sprite.is_active = False
        self.text_sprite.update_text(self.text_sprite.text)

    def commit_text(self, *, event: HashableEvent) -> None:
        """Commit the text typed into the text box: the one path for Enter and click-away.

        Valid text sets the value and tells the parent, so the color well and the canvas
        color follow; empty, unparsable or out-of-range text restores the value the box held
        when editing began. Either way the text box stops editing.

        Args:
            event: The event that commits the text (the Enter key, or the click elsewhere).

        """
        new_value = parse_channel(self.text_sprite.text, self.input_format)
        if new_value is None:
            self._restore_original_value()
            return

        self.value = new_value
        # Update original value for future restorations
        self.original_value = new_value
        self._notify_parent(event=event)

    def _notify_parent(self, *, event: HashableEvent) -> None:
        """Tell the parent the slider's value changed, so it can update its color.

        Args:
            event: The event that changed the value.

        """
        if self.parent is None:
            self.log.info('Slider %s has no parent to notify', self.name)
            return
        trigger = pygame.event.Event(0, {'name': self.name, 'value': self._value})
        self.parent.on_slider_event(event=event, trigger=trigger)

    def _set_value_from_mouse(self, event: HashableEvent) -> None:
        """Set the value from the mouse's x position on the slider and notify the parent.

        Args:
            event: The mouse event.

        """
        mouse_x = max(self.min_x, min(event.pos[0], self.max_x))
        self.value = ((mouse_x - self.min_x) * MAX_COLOR_CHANNEL_VALUE) // (self.max_x - self.min_x)
        self._notify_parent(event=event)

    def _handle_text_character_input(self, event: HashableEvent) -> None:
        """Handle character input in the slider text input."""
        if event.key == pygame.K_BACKSPACE:
            self.text_sprite.text = self.text_sprite.text[:-1]
        else:
            self.text_sprite.text += event.unicode.lower()

        # Limit to 3 characters to allow both "255" (decimal) and "FF" (hex)
        if len(self.text_sprite.text) > MAX_COLOR_TEXT_INPUT_LENGTH:
            self.text_sprite.text = self.text_sprite.text[:MAX_COLOR_TEXT_INPUT_LENGTH]

        # Force text sprite to update and redraw
        self.text_sprite.update_text(self.text_sprite.text)
        self.text_sprite.dirty = 2

    def update_slider_appearance(self) -> None:
        """Draw the slider's gradient on its image, column by column, and keep a copy of it."""
        for x in range(int(self.width)):
            intensity = int((x / self.width) * 255)
            if self.name == 'R':
                color = (intensity, 0, 0)
            elif self.name == 'G':
                color = (0, intensity, 0)
            elif self.name == 'B':
                color = (0, 0, intensity)
            else:
                color = (intensity, intensity, intensity)
            pygame.draw.line(self.image, color, (x, 0), (x, self.height))
        self._gradient = self.image.copy()
        # Copied back, never blended: on a display with per-pixel alpha (cocoa) the image takes
        # the display's format, and alpha-blending onto it leaves alpha 0, which the window
        # shows as black (glitchygames/opacity.py)
        self._gradient.set_alpha(None)
        self._gradient_drawn_on = self.image
        self._gradient_drawn_for = (self.width, self.height, self.name)

    def _current_gradient(self) -> pygame.Surface | None:
        """The kept gradient, when it was drawn for the slider's image, size and name.

        The slider is dirty every frame (dirty = 2), but its gradient depends only on these,
        so it is drawn column by column only when one of them changed; otherwise the kept copy
        repaints the image in one blit. The image holds only the gradient: the knob and the
        text box are sprites of their own.

        Returns:
            pygame.Surface | None: The kept gradient, or None when it must be drawn again.

        """
        if self._gradient_drawn_on is not self.image or self._gradient_drawn_for != (
            self.width,
            self.height,
            self.name,
        ):
            return None
        return self._gradient

    @override
    def on_left_mouse_button_down_event(self, event: MouseButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Handle left mouse button down event."""
        self.log.info('Slider %s mouse down event at %s, rect: %s', self.name, event.pos, self.rect)
        if self.rect.collidepoint(event.pos):
            self.log.info('Mouse down on slider %s', self.name)
            self.dragging = True
            self._set_value_from_mouse(event)
        else:
            self.log.info('Mouse click not on slider %s rect', self.name)

    @override
    def on_left_mouse_button_up_event(self, event: MouseButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Handle left mouse button up event."""
        self.log.info('Slider %s mouse up event', self.name)
        self.dragging = False

    @override
    def on_mouse_motion_event(self, event: MouseMotionEvent) -> None:
        """Handle mouse motion event."""
        if self.dragging:
            self.log.info('Dragging slider %s', self.name)
            self._set_value_from_mouse(event)

    @override
    def update(self) -> None:
        """Update the slider."""
        if self.dirty:
            gradient = self._current_gradient()
            if gradient is None:
                self.update_slider_appearance()
            else:
                self.image.blit(gradient, (0, 0))
        super().update()
        self.slider_knob.update()
        self.text_sprite.update()

def commit_text(self, *, event: HashableEvent) -> None:
    """Commit the text typed into the text box: the one path for Enter and click-away.

    Valid text sets the value and tells the parent, so the color well and the canvas
    color follow; empty, unparsable or out-of-range text restores the value the box held
    when editing began. Either way the text box stops editing.

    Args:
        event: The event that commits the text (the Enter key, or the click elsewhere).

    """
    new_value = parse_channel(self.text_sprite.text, self.input_format)
    if new_value is None:
        self._restore_original_value()
        return

    self.value = new_value
    # Update original value for future restorations
    self.original_value = new_value
    self._notify_parent(event=event)

def update_slider_appearance(self) -> None:
    """Draw the slider's gradient on its image, column by column, and keep a copy of it."""
    for x in range(int(self.width)):
        intensity = int((x / self.width) * 255)
        if self.name == 'R':
            color = (intensity, 0, 0)
        elif self.name == 'G':
            color = (0, intensity, 0)
        elif self.name == 'B':
            color = (0, 0, intensity)
        else:
            color = (intensity, intensity, intensity)
        pygame.draw.line(self.image, color, (x, 0), (x, self.height))
    self._gradient = self.image.copy()
    # Copied back, never blended: on a display with per-pixel alpha (cocoa) the image takes
    # the display's format, and alpha-blending onto it leaves alpha 0, which the window
    # shows as black (glitchygames/opacity.py)
    self._gradient.set_alpha(None)
    self._gradient_drawn_on = self.image
    self._gradient_drawn_for = (self.width, self.height, self.name)

class TabControlSprite(BitmappySprite):
    """A tab control sprite class."""

    log = LOG

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        x: int,
        y: int,
        width: int,
        height: int,
        *,
        name: str | None = None,
        parent: TabProtocol | None = None,
        groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize a TabControlSprite.

        Args:
            x (int): The x coordinate of the tab control sprite.
            y (int): The y coordinate of the tab control sprite.
            width (int): The width of the tab control sprite.
            height (int): The height of the tab control sprite.
            name (str | None): The name of the tab control sprite.
            parent (object | None): The parent object.
            groups (pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] | None): The sprite groups.

        """
        super().__init__(
            x=x,
            y=y,
            width=width,
            height=height,
            name=name,
            parent=parent,
            groups=groups,
        )

        # Tab options
        self.tabs: list[str] = [DECIMAL_INPUT_FORMAT, HEX_INPUT_FORMAT]
        self.active_tab: int = 0  # Start with %d (decimal)

        # Visual properties
        self.tab_height = height
        self.tab_width = width // len(self.tabs)
        self.border_color = (128, 128, 128)
        self.active_color = (200, 200, 200)
        self.inactive_color = (100, 100, 100)
        self.text_color = (0, 0, 0)

    @override
    def on_left_mouse_button_down_event(self: Self, event: MouseButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Handle left mouse button down event.

        Args:
            event (MouseButtonEvent): The pygame event.

        """
        if self.rect.collidepoint(event.pos):
            # Calculate which tab was clicked
            relative_x = int(event.pos[0] - self.rect.x)
            clicked_tab = relative_x // self.tab_width

            if 0 <= clicked_tab < len(self.tabs):
                self.active_tab = clicked_tab
                self.dirty = 2  # Force redraw
                self.log.info('Tab control: Switched to tab %s', self.tabs[self.active_tab])

                # Notify parent if it has a tab change handler
                if hasattr(self.parent, 'on_tab_change_event'):
                    self.parent.on_tab_change_event(self.tabs[self.active_tab])

    @override
    def update(self: Self) -> None:
        """Update the tab control sprite."""
        if self.dirty:
            # Clear the surface to black: the image has no SRCALPHA flag, so it is copied onto
            # the screen whole and was never transparent (alpha 0 only showed black on cocoa)
            self.image.fill((0, 0, 0))

            # Draw tabs
            for i, tab_text in enumerate(self.tabs):
                tab_x = i * self.tab_width
                tab_rect = pygame.Rect(tab_x, 0, self.tab_width, self.tab_height)

                # Choose colors based on active state
                bg_color = self.active_color if i == self.active_tab else self.inactive_color

                # Draw tab background
                pygame.draw.rect(self.image, bg_color, tab_rect)
                pygame.draw.rect(self.image, self.border_color, tab_rect, 1)

                # Draw tab text
                try:
                    font = pygame.font.Font(None, 16)
                    text_surface = font.render(tab_text, True, self.text_color)  # ruff: ignore[boolean-positional-value-in-call]
                    text_rect = text_surface.get_rect(center=tab_rect.center)
                    self.image.blit(text_surface, text_rect)
                except pygame.error, AttributeError:
                    # Handle font loading errors gracefully
                    pass

            # The text was alpha-blended onto the image, which leaves alpha 0 on a surface in the
            # format of a display with per-pixel alpha (cocoa's): black holes in the window
            make_opaque(surface=self.image)

def format_channel(value: int, input_format: str) -> str:
    """Format a color channel value for a slider text box.

    Args:
        value: The channel value (0-255).
        input_format: The text box format, HEX_INPUT_FORMAT or DECIMAL_INPUT_FORMAT.

    Returns:
        str: Two hex digits ('FF') in the hex format, otherwise decimal ('255').

    """
    if input_format == HEX_INPUT_FORMAT:
        return f'{value:02X}'
    return str(value)

def parse_channel(text: str, input_format: str) -> int | None:
    """Parse the text typed into a slider text box as a color channel value.

    The text is hex in the hex format (where "10" is 16, BUGS.md #110 item 3) or when it
    contains hex letters; otherwise it is decimal.

    Args:
        text: The typed text.
        input_format: The text box format, HEX_INPUT_FORMAT or DECIMAL_INPUT_FORMAT.

    Returns:
        int | None: The value, or None when the text is empty, unparsable or outside 0-255.

    """
    stripped_text = text.strip().lower()
    if not stripped_text:
        return None
    is_hex = input_format == HEX_INPUT_FORMAT or any(
        character in HEX_DIGIT_LETTERS for character in stripped_text
    )
    try:
        value = int(stripped_text, 16 if is_hex else 10)
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if not (0 <= value <= MAX_COLOR_CHANNEL_VALUE):
        return None
    return value
